'''''Xiangyunloong''''' ({{Lang-zh|s=祥云龙|t=祥雲龍|p=Xiángyúnlóng}}; meaning "auspicious cloud dragon") is a genus of [[massopoda]]n [[sauropodomorph]] dinosaur known from fossils found in the [[Early Jurassic]] [[Fengjiahe Formation]] of [[Yunnan]], China. The [[type species|type]] and [[Monotypic taxon|only species]] is '''''Xiangyunloong fengming'''''.<ref name=Xiangyunloong>{{Cite journal|last1=Hu |first1=S.-B. |last2=Wang |first2=Y.-C. |last3=Mo |first3=X. |last4=Zhang |first4=X.-Q. |last5=Zeng |first5=W.-T |last6=Wang |first6=T. |last7=Sun |first7=Z.-B |last8=Dong |first8=Q.-X. |last9=Guan |first9=Q. |last10=Liu |first10=Y.-H |last11=Zhang |first11=Y.-S. |last12=Bing |first12=Y. |last13=Wang |first13=Y.-M |last14=You |first14=H.-L |year=2026 |title=A new sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Lower Jurassic Fengjiahe Formation of Dali of Yunnan Province, China |journal=Royal Society Open Science |volume=13 |issue=3 |article-number=252219 |doi=10.1098/rsos.252219 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Discovery and naming ==
[[File:Xiangyunloong fengming (type locality).png|thumb|left|[[Type locality (biology)|Type locality]] in Yunnan, China]]
The [[holotype]], YDDY 10001–10041, is a partial skeleton including cervical, dorsal and caudal vertebrae, several dorsal rib fragments, chevrons, an incomplete left ilium, and a right ischium. It was discovered in [[Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture]], Yunnan Province, China.<ref name=Xiangyunloong />

It was [[species description|described]] as a new genus and species of sauropodomorph dinosaur in 2026. The [[generic name (biology)|generic name]], ''Xiangyunloong'', is a reference to [[Xiangyun County|Xiangyun]] ({{zh|s=祥云|t=祥雲|p=Xiángyún}}), the county where the holotype was discovered, with a name meaning "auspicious clouds". This is combined with the Chinese ''loong'' ({{Lang-zh|s=龙|t=龍|p=Lóng}}) or [[Chinese dragon]], a symbol of power and auspiciousness. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''fengming'', ({{Lang-zh|s=凤鸣|t=鳳鳴|p=Fèngmíng}}; literally "phoenix calling"), carries several meanings—it is a reference to Luming ({{Lang-zh|s=鹿鸣乡|t=鹿鳴鄉|p=Lùmíng Xiāng}}; literally "deer calling"), the town where the holotype was found, as well as a nod to the [[Feathered dinosaur|dinosaur–bird connection]]. "Fengming" is also the original name of Lin Fengmian, the founding president of China Academy of Art, whose staff participated extensively in the naming of the species.<ref name=Xiangyunloong />

== Description ==
[[File:Xiangyunloong fengming.png|thumb|[[Life restoration]]]]
Based on comparisons with the roughly coeval ''[[Lishulong]]'' and ''[[Xingxiulong yueorum]]'', the holotype individual of ''Xiangyunloong fengming'' has been estimated to have a body length of {{cvt|9|-|10|m|ft}}.<ref name=Xiangyunloong />

== Classification ==
To determine the relationships of ''Xiangyunloong'', Hu et al. scored it in the [[phylogenetic analysis]] of Wang et al. (2025).<ref name="Wudingloong">{{Cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Y.-M. |last2=Zhang |first2=Q.-N. |last3=Wang |first3=Y.-C. |last4=Xu |first4=H. |last5=Chen |first5=J. |last6=Feng |first6=Z. |last7=Xu |first7=X. |last8=Wang |first8=T. |last9=You |first9=H.-L. |year=2025 |title=A new Early Jurassic dinosaur represents the earliest-diverging and oldest sauropodomorph of East Asia |journal=[[Scientific Reports]] |volume=15 |issue=1 |article-number=26749 |doi=10.1038/s41598-025-12185-2 |doi-access=free |pmid=40702136 |pmc=12287354 |bibcode=2025NatSR..1526749W }}</ref> This analysis placed ''Xiangyunloong'' in an unresolved [[polytomy]] with both species of ''[[Xingxiulong]]''.
